effect: The starch is now individual glucose molecules that can cross the intestinal lining; the other foods still need breakdown.
reaction: The change from chains to individual molecules makes the purpose clear.
reason: The protein-digesting enzymes are pictured beside protein chains, so they are a clear match for the protein food.
expectation: The enzymes should break the protein into smaller pieces for absorption.

effect: The protein food has been broken into separate amino acids; the fat food still needs processing.
reaction: The amino acids connect digestion to the protein building blocks seen earlier.
reason: Bile and lipase are pictured working on fat droplets, making them the clear match for the fat food.
expectation: The fat should be broken down into smaller pieces for absorption.

effect: Fat digestion produced fatty acids and monoglycerides, completing the remaining goal. Bile disperses fat, while lipase breaks it apart.
reaction: The distinction between bile and lipase was useful; I hadn't known bile was not an enzyme.

mostWorthwhile.text: Breaking starch down in two stages was most worthwhile: the change from chains to individual glucose molecules made the purpose of digestion clear.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the three named organs was straightforward but a little repetitive; the explanation after the last fitting made their roles clearer.

surprise.text: I was surprised that bile helps disperse fat but is not the enzyme that breaks it apart. Monoglycerides were an unfamiliar term, though the picture showed them among the products.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt especially arbitrary: the slots and food-and-enzyme pictures pointed to the pairings, even when I didn't know all the details.

continue.text: I would continue to see how the small food products actually cross the gut lining, since this chapter prepared them for absorption but stopped before showing it.
